title: The Eucharist
hookLine: the source and summit of the Christian life (CCC 1324)

cards: A river starts somewhere small: a spring in the hills, a trickle coming up out of the ground. Every boat, mill and town downstream depends on that spring. A mountain works the other way round.
Its paths start in different valleys, on different sides, and every one of them is headed for the same place: the top.
The Catholic Church borrows those two pictures, source and summit, for one sacrament, and hangs the whole Christian life between them. Today, the Eucharist.

teach.b: Eucharist is a Greek word, eucharistia: thanksgiving. At the Last Supper, the Gospels say, Jesus took bread and gave thanks, and the sacrament takes its name from that thanks.
Earlier days walked through the Mass piece by piece, the consecration, and Justin's Sunday. Today's idea is bigger: where the Eucharist sits in everything else.
The Second Vatican Council called it the source and summit of the whole Christian life, and the Catechism repeats it in paragraph 1324.
Source: the other sacraments, the Church's work, a Catholic's prayer, all flow out of it, like a river from its spring.
Summit: they all lead back to it, like paths up a mountain. Baptism brings you to the table. Confirmation strengthens you to live what you receive there.
Confession clears the way back to it. Priests are ordained above all to celebrate it.
Catholics believe that in the Eucharist Jesus himself is truly present, body and blood, soul and divinity, which is why they call it the sacrament of sacraments. Paul adds another side in one line.
In the Douay-Rheims: "For we, being many, are one bread, one body, all that partake of one bread."

teach.h: WE, BEING MANY, ARE ONE BREAD, ONE BODY.
teach.b: The table doesn't only feed each person; it makes them one body. Day one hundred fourteen set out how other Christians understand the meal. All of them keep the table.

how: Catholics receive the Eucharist at Mass, which the Church asks them to attend each Sunday, after a first Communion in childhood, and fast for an hour beforehand.

o: a blessing said over the bread before supper
the thanksgiving meal where Catholics receive Christ
a memorial service held once a year at Easter

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: one body, all who share it

s: from the Greek eucharistia: at the Last Supper Jesus gave thanks.
the phrase source and summit comes from Vatican II
the Council used it, and the Catechism repeats it in paragraph 1324.
Catholics receive the Eucharist only once, like baptism
unlike baptism, it's received again and again: the table everything flows from and returns to.

games.q: it's the Last Supper. Jesus takes the bread. what does he do first?
games.why: he gives thanks, and the Greek word for that, eucharistein, gave the sacrament its name.

practice: Let two words ride your breathing: source on the in-breath, the spring your day comes out of, whether rest, love, a person or God, and summit on the out-breath, what your day is really climbing toward.
Don't answer quickly; just let the two words go back and forth. If you pray, give thanks, which is what the word Eucharist means.

wordCard.voice: The Eucharist. From the Greek for thanksgiving. For Catholics, the source that everything flows from, and the summit everything climbs toward. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: thanksgiving. Built from eu, good, and charis, grace or gift.

carryVoice: Your line: everything flows from the table. And everything climbs back to it. Day one hundred twenty-eight, done.
